snapshot.title: UPSC Environment: Ecology & Ecosystems
snapshot.exam_hook: 🏔️ UPSC Environment Hook: Ecotone: Edge effect. 10% Law: Energy loss. Mutualism: Lichen. Niche: Role. Pioneer: Lichen. Tansley: Ecosystem.

quick_notes.title: Basic Concepts
quick_notes.detail: Ecology (Haeckel). Ecosystem (Tansley). Ecocline : Gradual transition between two ecosystems. Ecotone : Sharp transition zone (e.g., Mangroves).

quick_notes.title: Ecological Niche
quick_notes.detail: The unique functional role of a species in its ecosystem (where it lives and what it does). No two species can have the same niche (Competitive Exclusion Principle).

quick_notes.title: Energy Flow
quick_notes.detail: Unidirectional flow. Lindeman's 10 percent law says only about one-tenth of energy passes from one trophic level to the next (Lindeman): Only 10% of energy is transferred to the next trophic level. Energy decreases as we go up.

quick_notes.title: Biotic Interactions
quick_notes.detail: 1. Mutualism (+/+): Both benefit (Lichen). 2. Commensalism (+/0): One benefits, other unaffected (Barnacles on whale). 3. Parasitism (+/-): One benefits at others cost. 4. Amensalism (-/0): One harmed, other unaffected.

quick_notes.title: Ecological Succession
quick_notes.detail: Primary: On bare rock (Lichen as pioneer). Secondary : On already existing soil (after fire/flood). Seral stages lead to a Climax Community.

lesson_intro: Today we study the 'Web of Life'. Ecology is the study of how organisms interact with their environment. We explore the components of an ecosystem, the flow of energy through 'Trophic Levels', and the various 'Biotic Interactions' (Mutualism, Parasitism). For UPSC, focus on 'Ecological Niche', 'Ecological Succession', and the '10% Law of Energy Transfer'. This is the foundation of environmental science.
